title: Lesson 2 - Data 360 Business Value and Positioning: CDP, Data Silos, Credits, and Data Cloud One
description: Describe Data 360's key terminology and business value, covering the business case a consultant must make (data silos, the Salesforce-native CDP position, credits and consumption, and the Data Cloud One multi-org model).

questions.question: A services organization wants one customer view shared by sales, service, and marketing, plus trusted context for its AI agents. Which positioning statement is correct?
options: Data 360 is the Salesforce-native data platform that unifies data and powers AI across sales, service, marketing, and commerce
Data 360 is a data warehouse that stores all raw enterprise data
Data 360 is a business intelligence tool
questions.explanation: Data 360 is Salesforce-native and spans functions plus Agentforce grounding. The strongest distractor limits it to marketing, which is exactly the positioning mistake that undersells the platform.

questions.question: Which statement about Data 360 consumption is TRUE?
options: Flex Credits cannot be used for Data 360 work
Credits are unlimited once the product is licensed
Data 360 is consumption-based: actions generate usage events that consume credits by usage type
Credits are consumed only for data storage
questions.explanation: Pricing is consumption-based and each action has a usage type that decrements credits. Flex Credits are interchangeable across Data 360 and Agentforce, so the last option is wrong.

questions.question: An enterprise has five Salesforce orgs and wants one governed Data 360 instance. Which approach does Salesforce recommend?
options: Federate all five orgs with Zero Copy instead of licensing Data 360
Replicate Data 360 metadata manually between orgs
Buy five Data 360 licenses, one per org
Use Data Cloud One with one home org hosting Data 360 and the other orgs as companion orgs
questions.explanation: Each org can hold only one Data 360 license and Salesforce recommends Data Cloud One for multiple orgs, so one home org with companion orgs is the pattern. The first option multiplies cost and fragments governance.
